evidence.summary: Tuvok and Chakotay return injured; the Doctor reports Chakotay's bio-neural energy has been extracted and his body is brain-dead while remaining physiologically supported.
Tuvok reports that an unidentified ship attacked their shuttle after emerging from the nebula.
evidence.counterevidence: Later reconstructed sensor data show no attacking ship and identify the energy discharge as originating from the nebula.

evidence.summary: Kes performs/assists with Chakotay's medicine-wheel tradition and later senses an unexplained presence.
evidence.counterevidence: The ritual explanation is cultural/experiential evidence, not independent proof of a soul or displaced consciousness.

evidence.summary: Voyager repeatedly changes course or loses systems through actions attributed to crew locations; forensic scans find anomalous memory patterns superimposed on Paris and Torres during actions they deny performing.
The Doctor hypothesizes that an unknown noncorporeal entity can temporarily control organic crew members.
evidence.counterevidence: At this stage the mechanism and number of entities are not established.

evidence.summary: Janeway transfers command-code fail-safe authority to the Doctor because available evidence suggests the organic senior officers may be compromised.
Kes and Tuvok are attacked; Kes's neck injuries are later identified as physical trauma consistent with a Vulcan neck pinch, raising the possibility that Tuvok acted while controlled.
The Doctor is disabled and Janeway divides command protocols between herself and Tuvok so that no single organic host holds all command authority.
Torres reconstructs the shuttle logs and finds there was no alien ship; the discharge came from the nebula, contradicting Tuvok's earlier account.
Tuvok attempts to take command and continue into the nebula; energy beings identify themselves as Komar while a separate anomalous action ejects the warp core using Chakotay's command authorization.

The crew infers two distinct presences: a Komar-controlled Tuvok driving Voyager inward and a Chakotay-linked presence acting through others to resist; rearranged medicine-wheel stones provide a route out of the nebula.
After the Doctor reintegrates him, Chakotay reports feeling outside his body and learning to share the consciousness of nearby people in order to act.
evidence.counterevidence: This establishes the episode's reported/depicted consciousness model, not a general metaphysical theory of minds independent of bodies.

assertions.subject: voy-cath:chakotay_consciousness
counterevidence: Reintegration and self-report support the work-local relation, but do not settle a broader metaphysical identity rule.

assertions.subject: voy-cath:medicine_wheel
counterevidence: The artifact's ritual meaning and its later pragmatic use are distinct; no general supernatural property is inferred.

neutral_coding.plot_problem: A supposed external attack becomes a possession/control crisis involving two competing noncorporeal presences and compromised command authority.
neutral_coding.identity_epistemics: Chakotay's supported body and displaced consciousness are represented separately without forcing a global body-mind identity rule.
neutral_coding.epistemics: Tuvok's initial testimony is preserved and explicitly contradicted by later sensor reconstruction rather than silently overwritten.
neutral_coding.counterevidence: Kes's ritual perceptions and Chakotay's later self-report support the source-local consciousness account but do not establish universal metaphysical claims.
